quote: **Consultant draft.** The secure-memory requirements come from the dated coordinator rulings. The proposed W3 screens, status codes, command names, strict-only package, hardware baseline and transfer workflow are recommendations for review. The base recommendation is in [B6](../B6-base-memo.md). B36 settled the network markers. Each contract row below is one acceptance requirement. The identifier at the right names the test and the last column gives its expected observation.

Assemble two amd64 images from one pinned Debian 13 snapshot pair and one authenticated Linux source revision, using distinct kernel configurations, package lists, OS identities and artifact names. Both role manifests resolve, the stick and node kernels differ, and substituting either kernel for the other fails.

On the sitting stick compile loopback, local Unix sockets, USB host, HID, mass storage and CDC-ACM into the kernel and exclude network device drivers, wireless, USB networking, DVB, loadable modules, swap, hibernation and kernel core dumps. The resolved configuration, linked kernel and unpacked boot and root filesystems agree, the guest sees the emulated Ethernet controller and virtio network function without binding a network driver (the virtio PCI transport may bind), and adding USB Ethernet leaves exactly lo.

The stick sets ID=mr-sitting-stick and a kernel release ending in -mr-sitting, and W1 independently checks those markers and the running network property. The packaged helper recognizes both correct markers with only lo, and each wrong marker or extra interface fails W1's B34 recognition.

Boot the verified medium without mounting other storage, select its immutable system, use RAM for all session writes including /run, the private XDG runtime, home, /tmp, logs and the live overlay, and disable persistence, resume and system crash capture. A VM with writable internal storage, a pre-attached transfer medium and a swap partition shows zero mounts of all three at startup, zero active swap, volatile sessions across cold boots and unchanged disk hashes.

Before starting any holder application, check the sitting identity, exact interface set, resolved running kernel policy, immutable strict-helper identity, mount policy and the session's exact limits, and fail closed on any missing or unreadable required evidence. Each failed check returns 2, writes the applicable Boot message once and starts no GUI or helper, while the clean image starts the graphical session.

Start an unprivileged local Wayland session with mr-gui as the first application, a working OS folder picker and a private writable sitting folder in RAM. The actual wallet appears, the folder picker can select the RAM folder, and the unsynced offline wallet can export a signet plan there.

Give the session controls named “Transfer files” and “Power off”, start the existing W2 terminal through I6, retain its argv boundaries and cleaned environment, and return to the wallet after the terminal closes. A real wallet export whose folder contains spaces reaches the packaged helper and returns to the wallet, the cleared GUI-only variable is absent in the helper, and Power off requires confirmation.

The secret-free node foundation uses ID=refugium-node and a distinct kernel suffix -mr-node, shares the I5 untrusted mount policy, and excludes mr-sitting and its terminal launch entry. The booted node identifies its role, cannot start a sitting, and accepts a requested read-only transfer without automounting it.

**Boot messages.** For B05, the first applicable failure wins in this order. The diagnostic is one line on the local console. Failure leaves the machine at that line for power-off and does not launch a login shell.
Boot identity or kernel policy cannot be established `This stick could not verify its offline kernel. Power off and boot a verified Refugium sitting stick.`
Network interfaces differ from lo, or enumeration fails `This stick could not verify that networking is disabled. Power off and boot a verified Refugium sitting stick.`
Swap, volatile storage or mount checks fail `This stick could not verify its RAM-only session. Power off and boot a verified Refugium sitting stick.`
Strict helper or memory limits fail `This stick could not verify its memory protection. Power off and boot a verified Refugium sitting stick.`
The graphical session cannot start or its initial wallet process fails to start `Refugium Wallet could not start. Power off and try a supported display and USB keyboard.`

Give the unprivileged session, mr-gui, terminal and direct and GUI-launched mr-sitting soft and hard RLIMIT_MEMLOCK of exactly 67108864 bytes without CAP_IPC_LOCK. Each live process reports both limits and no bypass capability, including direct invocation with its environment cleared.

Build the stick's mr-sitting with strict-only policy and require successful mlockall(MCL_CURRENT plus MCL_FUTURE) before any secret prompt, input, derivation or display on sit, verify, root and child. With the normal limit the helper locks current and newly allocated test pages, while with insufficient limit each entry refuses with D06 and exit 2 before consuming input, including line mode and direct launch. A request for ordinary best effort on the stick exits 2 without reading input.

Keep the lock while secrets are live and through controlled cleanup, reserve cleanup and message storage before accepting secrets, and never invoke the ordinary allocator's unlock-and-retry behavior in the strict helper. A controlled post-entry allocation failure reaches D07 and exit 1, the lock remains active through final cleanup, the owning threads wipe their buffers and private plate material is removed, with no munlockall or allocator abort.

If the closing worker cannot start but the sitting can safely wait, retain the lock and the written hand-back and show the existing wallet-check retry and quit choices. Forced spawn failure shows “The wallet check did not run.” with unchanged hand-back bytes, retry can succeed, and quit completes cleanup.

Report only confirmed cleanup on handled exits and acknowledge that the displaying terminal can retain text; an uncatchable kill produces no cleanup success message. Normal completion and handled termination clean up while locked, a partial cleanup never prints an unqualified success, and SIGKILL produces no final report from the process.

Configure the packaged Alacritty with zero scrollback, disabled OSC 52, no IPC socket or live reload, RAM-only diagnostic output and an immutable configuration selected by the image-owned terminal launcher. Actual terminal history is zero after overflow, resize and alternate-screen return, a ten-line control retains history, a working AT-SPI observer sees its positive-control label and no terminal text object, and the launcher rejects emulator option injection.

Package the real signet-capable sitting, wallet, mr, engraving CLI and patched libusb-enabled picotool from pinned artifacts, leaving Bitcoin Core and all node receiver software off the stick. Installed executable hashes and versions, package closure and shared libraries match the release inputs, with real binaries for continued execution and no node daemon.

Run the maximum supported signet sitting through the packaged GUI, its terminal and its closing check at the shipping limit and record the highest observed locked KiB. The hand-back matches its plan, the closing check completes, the lock stays held until cleanup and neither secret material nor private runtime files reach storage or the test report.

**Proposed strict failure texts.** D06 is a helper diagnostic before any secret and D07 is the heading for a controlled stop after entry. The existing helper owns its other screens, all successful end wording and quit keys. If a controlled cleanup cannot be confirmed, the helper must report that outcome. A failure message must not echo secret input.
Initial strict lock or cleanup reservation fails `mr-sitting could not secure its memory. No secret was read. Restart the sitting stick and try again.`
The strict session cannot safely continue while locked `This sitting cannot continue with its memory locked. Stopping and cleaning up.`

The W3 screen title is **Transfer files**. Its actions are **Read a plan**, **Save public files**, **Eject** and **Back**. **Choose a drive** lists eligible drives by port, capacity and an opaque current selection identifier. **Choose a public file** lists eligible canonical filenames for the chosen operation. Neither selector preselects an item. **Cancel** returns to the previous screen. After a successful import the screen offers **Open sitting** or **Back**. **Open sitting** launches the same image terminal with the real helper and the imported plan, RAM hand-back path and, where required by the plan, its W1 closing paths. A hot plan created elsewhere still requires its matching public closing request to complete the optional wallet check; no portable closing protocol is added in W3. Choosing **Power off** shows **Power off this stick? Files left only in RAM will be lost.** with **Cancel** initially selected and **Power off** as the other choice. A power-off request ends the graphical session through normal termination before shutting down. Selecting a drive uses its display identifier, size and port. Port and device identity are resolved again at the point of use. An input plan on another computer is already public. The holder's session folder is independent of the source drive.

Enumerate USB partitions without mounting them, select explicitly, exclude every partition of the boot disk and all internal volumes, refuse ambiguous or changed device identity and refuse unsupported filesystems. Two eligible USB partitions stay unmounted on insertion, no default action chooses either, and the wrong device, unsupported filesystem and replacement cases give D09 or D10 with no I/O to those devices.

Import only a regular public I1 plan from the chosen FAT32 source mounted read-only,nosuid,nodev,noexec, validate it with the pinned W1 codec, create its canonical file without overwriting anything in the RAM sitting folder and leave source bytes unchanged. The valid plan appears byte-for-byte in RAM, Open sitting uses its actual plan-dependent paths, and directory traversal, malformed input, file collision and a pulled device report D11, D12 or D13.

Export only the selected canonical public I1 or matched I2 from the RAM sitting folder using its pinned codec and exact plan binding, after the holder confirms a separate designated FAT32 output medium; never make untrusted input writable. Valid files can leave the stick with private ownership semantics, while malformed or mismatched data, private plate files, symlinks, arbitrary paths, input media and existing destinations cannot be exported or overwritten.

Use restrictive permissions and nosuid,nodev,noexec for the output mount, deny general GUI access to the writable mount, finish and flush each new file before success, and preserve prior complete files after interruption or retry. Killing or unplugging during a copy cannot replace an existing file or yield D14, a clean retry can finish, and successful eject unmounts before D15.

Give the holder access to the supported BOOTSEL device through usbfs and CDC-ACM as separate functions, and keep BOOTSEL, ECM and RNDIS devices out of the transfer-mount path. A read-only picotool info operation works on the target, a synthetic serial exchange works via CDC-ACM, and USB Ethernet and the BOOTSEL storage presentation produce no automatic mount or network interface.

**Transfer responses.** Navigation and cancellation return to the wallet or transfer screen without performing an operation. Success, refusal or cancellation from an invoked transfer operation returns 0, 2 or 1 respectively. A run-time I/O failure returns 1. For a transfer, the check order is selection, identity and role, filesystem, source validation, collision, confirmation for export, then I/O.
No eligible drive `Connect a USB transfer drive, then select it here.`
Ineligible, ambiguous or changed device `This drive cannot be used for this transfer. Select the intended USB drive again.`
Unsupported filesystem `This stick accepts FAT32 transfer drives. Choose another drive.`
Invalid, unsafe or mismatched public file `This file is not a valid public plan or matching hand-back. No file was copied.`
Name collision `A file with this name already exists. It was left unchanged.`
I/O failure or removal `The transfer did not finish. Reconnect the drive and check its files before trying again.`
Successful export after durable write and unmount `Public file saved. You can remove the transfer drive.`
Successful eject `Drive ejected. You can remove it.`
Confirmation for export `Save this public file to the selected output drive?` with `Save` and `Cancel`, initially on `Cancel`
Successful import `Plan copied to the sitting folder in RAM.`

Acquire pinned inputs on the connected builder, verify archive authentication and hashes, bind each application to its source, build recipe, lockfile, artifact and license, and refuse a missing or altered mandatory input before producing a release image. The complete authenticated input set passes, each absence or alteration fails with D18, and selecting another role's inputs is refused.

Build both roles twice in independent clean VMs from the same locked inputs and compare all bytes of each final bootable image, including its boot records. Both builds return identical byte counts and SHA-256 per role, with different hashes between roles, and a one-byte change is detected.

On a separate computer verify a signed manifest against the independently acquired release key, the requested role and version, exact byte length and SHA-256 before a write, and check the image-length readback after writing a replacement drive. Wrong signer, role, version, length, content and short readback give D19 or D20, no preverification failure writes a device, and bytes beyond the declared extent do not affect readback.

Claim physical support only for individually recorded x86-64 UEFI machines that boot, display the GUI and terminal, accept USB HID, enforce network and mount rules and operate the specified serial and BOOTSEL devices. Record the exact Intel and AMD models, firmware settings, ports and operation results in a physical run before listing them as supported, separately from the OVMF and virtual GPU result.
Release input verification fails `A required image input is missing or failed verification.`
Release manifest or image verification fails `Image verification failed. No drive was written.`
Written extent differs or cannot be read `The written drive could not be verified. Keep the previous stick.`

The build and verification tools identify the failed stage and exit without signing or publishing when a required guest, release input or physical result is missing. Build and verification tools use status 0 for success, 1 for failed operational verification and 2 for an invalid invocation. Physical firmware messages before the image receives control belong to the machine. The wallet, W1's existing screens and W6's future engraving dialogue retain their originating specifications. Signet fixtures exercise wallet behavior. Hardware probes use public non-wallet data. The node's Core, satellite receiver, signing software and encrypted data-partition provisioning remain the responsibility of W4, W5 and W7 under the umbrella design.

The proposed B6 base, the strict-only image package, Alacritty, FAT32 transfers, the hardware matrix and the release trust key are discussed in the [design draft](../W3-stick-design-draft.md). The proposed v1 compatibility promise covers a verified image on tested UEFI hardware with its tested boot policy; requiring Secure Boot with a project-enrolled trust chain is an owner decision before a public release. Approval of B6 by itself qualifies neither a device nor a release. Production signatures and real hardware results are supplied in the release process.
